description:
The Vishist Coaching Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India under the aegis of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

This scheme was specifically designed to provide coaching and financial assistance to the children of construction workers. 

The scheme was launched in the year 2019. 

It aims to enhance the educational opportunities for the children of workers in the construction sector. 

The primary objective of the Vishist Coaching Scheme is to provide financial support for coaching classes to children who are preparing for competitive examinations. 

These examinations include those for professional courses such as engineering and medical colleges. 

The scheme targets children from families who are registered under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act 1996. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is up to INR 50,000 per child. 

This amount can be utilized for coaching fees, study materials, and other related expenses. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for children who are in the 11th and 12th grades. 

It aims to support students who are aspiring to enter prestigious institutions through competitive exams. 

The eligibility criteria for the Vishist Coaching Scheme are clearly defined. 

Applicants must be children of registered construction workers. 

The age limit for applicants is typically between 16 to 25 years. 

The family income of the construction worker should not exceed INR 8,000 per month. 

This income criterion ensures that the benefits reach those who are genuinely in need. 

To apply for the Vishist Coaching Scheme, applicants must follow a specific process. 

The first step is to fill out the application form available through state-level Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Boards. 

The application form requires details such as the applicant's name, age, educational qualifications, and the name of the construction worker parent. 

Applicants must also provide proof of their parent’s registration as a construction worker. 

Documents required for the application include a copy of the construction worker's registration certificate. 

Additionally, applicants must submit their educational certificates. 

A recent passport-sized photograph is also required. 

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the respective state welfare board. 

The timeline for the application process varies by state. 

Generally, applications are accepted throughout the year. 

However, specific deadlines may be set for each academic year. 

Disbursement of funds under the scheme typically occurs soon after the application is approved. 

The funds are directly transferred to the bank account of the applicant. 

This ensures that the financial assistance is received promptly. 

The implementing authority for the Vishist Coaching Scheme is the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

Each state has its own board that oversees the implementation of this scheme. 

These boards are responsible for processing applications and disbursing funds. 

For any queries or assistance, applicants can contact the respective state welfare board. 

The contact details for these boards can be found on the official Ministry of Labour and Employment website. 

The Vishist Coaching Scheme is part of a broader effort by the Indian government to improve educational outcomes for marginalized communities. 

By focusing on children of construction workers, the scheme aims to break the cycle of poverty. 

It provides opportunities for higher education and better career prospects. 

The scheme has been well-received since its inception. 

Many families have benefited from the financial assistance provided. 

The scheme has also raised awareness about the importance of education among construction workers. 

In terms of statistics, the scheme has supported thousands of students since its launch. 

The exact number of beneficiaries varies by state and year. 

However, reports indicate a steady increase in the number of applications received each year. 

The success of the scheme can be attributed to its targeted approach. 

By focusing on a specific demographic, the government ensures that resources are allocated efficiently. 

The Vishist Coaching Scheme also aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

It promotes quality education and aims to ensure inclusive and equitable education for all. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to social welfare and education. 

In conclusion, the Vishist Coaching Scheme serves as a vital resource for the children of construction workers. 

It provides them with the necessary financial support to pursue their educational aspirations. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to empower a vulnerable section of society. 

The scheme not only enhances individual prospects but also contributes to the overall development of communities. 

As the scheme continues to evolve, it is expected to reach even more beneficiaries in the coming years. 

The Vishist Coaching Scheme exemplifies the importance of targeted welfare initiatives in promoting education. 

It stands as a model for similar programs aimed at uplifting marginalized communities across India. 

The ongoing support and improvements to the scheme will ensure its sustainability and effectiveness. 

Overall, the Vishist Coaching Scheme is a significant step towards achieving educational equity in India.
